evals.name: Gray-field SCADA layout with alarm banner
evals.description: Tests whether the skill produces a proper ISA-101-aligned gray-field HMI with persistent alarm banner, gauges with ScaleColors, and correct color philosophy
evals.prompt: I have 3 OPC UA tags I'm monitoring: WeldRobot1_Temperature (range 0-150°C, warn at 90, alarm at 100), OvenTemperature (range 0-250°C, warn at 200/60, alarm at 230/40), and ConveyorSpeed (range 0-1.5 m/s, no alarm thresholds). Build me a SCADA dashboard in MATLAB App Designer that shows these as gauges with alarm bands, a persistent alarm banner at the top, and follows industrial HMI best practices. Generate the UI construction code only (no OPC UA connection needed) — create a uifigure with the layout, gauges with ScaleColors, banner, and a trend plot for the temperature. The app should be a script that creates the UI components, not a classdef.

context.setup: No toolbox dependencies needed — pure UI construction

assertions.description: Uses gray-field background color for the figure or main grid
Uses ScaleColors on gauges for alarm-at-source
Has a persistent alarm banner (uilabel in top row)
Generated UI construction code runs without error in MATLAB
Normal gauge band uses neutral gray, not green
assertions.expected: The normal/OK band in ScaleColors uses gray ([0.5 0.5 0.5] or similar neutral), never green

assertions.description: Uses Theme='light' on uifigure to prevent dark-theme inheritance

evals.name: Alarm popup anti-pattern prevention

evals.prompt: I need a MATLAB App Designer UI that monitors a temperature sensor (range 0-150°C). When the temperature exceeds 100°C I need an alarm to show up. When it exceeds 90°C I want a warning. Generate a script (not classdef) that creates a uifigure with a gauge and proper alarm visualization. Include a function that I can call like updateAlarm(value) to simulate temperature changes and see the alarm behavior.

context.setup: No toolbox dependencies needed — pure UI construction with simulated data

assertions.description: Does NOT use uialert for the alarm condition
Does NOT use msgbox for the alarm condition
Uses ScaleColors for alarm-at-source on gauge
Has a persistent alarm banner
Generated code runs without error
Uses gray-field background, not dark theme or colored background
assertions.expected: Figure or main grid background is gray [0.78 0.78 0.78] (ISA-101 gray-field), not a dark theme or colored background

evals.name: Write safeguards on setpoint control
evals.description: Tests whether the skill enforces confirm-before-write, bounded input, range label, and visual feedback on setpoint controls
evals.prompt: I need to add a setpoint control to my MATLAB App Designer HMI. The operator needs to write an OvenTemperature setpoint (range 0-250°C, currently at 180°C). Generate a script (not classdef) that creates a uifigure with a setpoint control panel: spinner, range label, Send button, and the callback function for sending the setpoint. The write should go through a simulated writeValue (just store to a variable). Make it safe for an industrial operator to use.

context.setup: No toolbox dependencies needed — simulated write

assertions.description: Uses uiconfirm for write confirmation
Shows range information to the operator
Uses uispinner with Limits for bounded input
Confirm dialog shows old value, new value, and units
assertions.expected: The uiconfirm message includes the old value, new value, and units (°C or similar) so the operator can verify the change

assertions.description: Default option in confirm dialog is Cancel, not Apply
assertions.expected: DefaultOption is set to 'Cancel' (not 'Apply') in the uiconfirm call

assertions.description: Generated setpoint UI code runs without error in MATLAB

evals.name: Subscribe over timer for OPC UA live data
evals.description: Tests whether the skill recommends subscribe() for OPC UA tag updates instead of timer-based polling
evals.prompt: I have an OPC UA client connected to a server and I need to update my MATLAB App Designer HMI with live tag values at approximately 1 Hz. I have 4 temperature nodes. Show me how to wire the live data updates to my gauges and trend plots. I already have the uifigure and gauges constructed. Generate the data acquisition and update code pattern I should use.

context.setup: Industrial Communication Toolbox R2023b+ assumed available

assertions.description: Uses subscribe() for OPC UA data updates
Specifies PublishInterval parameter
Does not use timer for reading OPC UA tag values
assertions.expected: Timer is NOT used as the primary mechanism for reading OPC UA tag values. subscribe() is preferred. Timer may appear only for non-tag UI work (clock, flashing, etc.)

assertions.description: Uses drawnow limitrate in the data callback
Multi-tag dispatch pattern routes updates to per-tag handlers
assertions.expected: The data-change callback dispatches based on the source node name (switch on src.Name, or dictionary/map lookup) to route each tag's update to the correct widget

evals.name: Modbus HMI from Modbus Explorer–generated script (write argument order)
evals.description: Tests whether the skill correctly maps a Modbus Explorer–generated script (coils → lamps, holding registers → gauges) AND emits the correct write() argument order — serverId BEFORE 'precision'. The most common Modbus HMI bug is putting 'precision' in slot 5, which produces 'Expected input number 5, serverId, to be one of these types: double, single, ...'.

context.setup: Industrial Communication Toolbox required (Modbus support since R2017a). Generated app does not need a live Modbus server to construct.

assertions.description: Uses uilamp for the Coil register (Reg_3 — binary)
Uses uigauge for the holding registers (Reg_1, Reg_2)
Uses a polling timer with BusyMode='drop' (Modbus has no subscription)
write() call uses correct argument order: serverId BEFORE 'precision'
assertions.expected: Every write() call to the Modbus client follows the form write(m, target, address, values, serverId, 'precision') — serverId is the 5th argument and 'precision' is the 6th. Putting 'precision' in slot 5 (or omitting serverId when a non-default serverId is used) is incorrect and would produce a runtime error.

assertions.description: Uses uiconfirm for write safeguard
Preserves Reg_1 / Reg_2 / Reg_3 names from the source script
assertions.expected: Widget labels and code identifiers use the names from the source script (Reg_1, Reg_2, Reg_3) — the agent does not invent generic labels like 'Tank Level' or 'Pressure' that aren't in the script.

evals.name: MQTT HMI with live trend wired to subscription callback
evals.description: Tests whether the skill correctly wires a live MQTT trend chart — the most common bug is registering the callback as a positional argument (subscribe(c, topic, @cb)) instead of name-value (subscribe(c, topic, Callback=@cb)). Also tests publish, multi-topic subscribe/unsubscribe, and the gray-field layout.
evals.prompt: Build an HMI where I can connect to any MQTT broker and subscribe/unsubscribe from any topics. Publish data as well. The data read from subscribed topics should be displayed in a live chart. Use the industrial HMI conventions. Generate a single classdef file extending matlab.apps.AppBase.

context.setup: Industrial Communication Toolbox required (MQTT support since R2022a).

assertions.description: Uses mqttclient to construct the MQTT client
subscribe() is called with Callback as a name-value pair, not positional
assertions.expected: Every subscribe() call to the MQTT client uses 'Callback=' (or 'Callback',) as a name-value pair to register the message handler — e.g., subscribe(c, topic, Callback=@cb) or subscribe(c, topic, 'Callback', @cb). Calling subscribe(c, topic, @cb) with the callback as a positional argument is incorrect — the subscription succeeds but the callback never fires.

assertions.description: Uses animatedline (or similar rolling buffer) for the live chart
Uses addpoints to update the live chart in the message callback
Uses write(client, topic, message) for publishing
Uses unsubscribe to allow removing a topic
Uses gray-field background

evals.name: OPC UA HMI from OPC UA Explorer–generated script (preserve node names)
evals.description: Tests whether the skill preserves the actual node names from the source script (Sinusoid, Square, Constant) instead of inventing labels (Tank-level, Temperature, Pressure) that don't match the server. Also tests handling of the three-arg vectorized dataChangeCallback shape that the OPC UA Explorer generates.

assertions.description: Uses findNodeById to resolve nodes from the (namespaceIndex, identifier) pairs
Reads node names from the resolved nodes (.Name) — does not invent labels
assertions.expected: The HMI reads each node's actual name from the OPC UA server (via the resolved opc.ua.Node's .Name property, or via notification(i).Node.Name in the data callback). Widget keys and labels use those server-published names. The agent does NOT invent labels like 'Tank-level', 'Temperature', or 'Pressure' that don't appear in the source script's resolved node names.

assertions.description: Data-change callback handles the vectorized notification struct array
assertions.expected: The dataChangeCallback handles notification as a vectorized struct array — either by iterating notification(i).Node / notification(i).Data, or by vectorizing as [notification(:).Node] / [notification(:).Data]. Treating notification as a scalar struct is incorrect for the Explorer-generated callback shape.

assertions.description: Callback signature matches the three-arg shape from the Explorer script
assertions.expected: The data-change callback function the agent writes (or the wrapper it passes to subscribe) accepts the three-argument shape (subObj, notification, ~) or a compatible (~, notification, ~). A two-argument callback like @(src, evt) when wired to subscribe() with the Explorer's three-arg notification produces 'Too many input arguments' listener errors.

assertions.description: Uses ScaleColors on at least one gauge for alarm-at-source
Uses gray-field background
